question.problem:
Which of the three sequences below are arithmetic sequences?

I. $-2,\,-4,\,-6,\,-8,...$

II. $-2,\,-9,\,-16,\,-23,...$

III. $-2,\,4,\,10,\,16,...$
question.worked_solution:
To determine whether each sequence is an arithmetic sequence, we need to look at the jumps between terms in the sequence. If the jumps are the same, then they indeed represent a common difference of an arithmetic sequence. 

- In sequence I, the jumps are all the same. Therefore, sequence I is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=-2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203588/assets/c599604e6630b0dbf74d646f93b6330b5d310f35bfbce7b008f16d1686534c77.png)

- In sequence II, the jumps are all the same. Therefore, sequence II is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=-7.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203588/assets/b35cc27bfa6f7fe2171529a0c84e9ab8d33c122e932512fae1b06fe21cc9bc94.png)

- In sequence III, the jumps are all the same. Therefore, sequence III is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=6.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203588/assets/9aa43107c2b5c975450590f4bc126273b45ddc72f1acfd3d35eadff0313ded1b.png)

In conclusion, sequences I, II, and III are arithmetic sequences.
